Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The authors caution that a single-platform, geographically uneven sample and only 36 behavioral participants limit generalization; language ratings with fewer than three respondents are individual observations, and model changes can age these ratings.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The study combines a 64-question questionnaire with a task in which selected multilingual writers prompt an AI chatbot for a local-event advertisement, revise it and submit the interaction and versions; two analysts inductively code free-text responses and resolve disagreements by discussion.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The questionnaire includes 301 Toloka freelance writers from 49 countries; the interactive task includes 36 participants selected from 120 invitations using language proficiency, low self-ratings and/or detailed comments.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Among the surveyed professional writers, 73% report using AI chatbots; the paper reports that 75% improve outputs through iterative prompting and audience specification, as a sample-specific self-reported practice.
